reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Mastectomy after neoadjuvant chemo with new cardiotoxicity (EF 62 to 40%), neutropenia, QTc 484 with low Mg and an ondansetron QT intolerance, very high PONV risk, no IV access with the left arm off limits, and isosulfan blue planned.

asa.rationale: Cancer therapy related cardiac dysfunction (EF 40%) with symptoms, neutropenia, prolonged QT.

decision.recommendation: proceed with modifications if same day issues are resolved
decision.rationale: Cancer surgery timing matters, but before induction: repeat CBC with ANC today (10/26 draw missed), replete magnesium, quick cardiology input on new HFrEF, IV access via the port, and a non 5HT3 PONV plan.

redFlags.finding: New cancer therapy related cardiac dysfunction
redFlags.evidence: EF 62% (05/2026) to 40% (10/20), GLS -12%, BNP 240 to 310, DOE and ankle swelling, HR about 100; cardio oncology not until 11/18.
redFlags.implication: New HFrEF, not on guideline therapy.
redFlags.action: Cardiology input before induction, careful titration, avoid myocardial depression and fluid overload.

redFlags.evidence: QTc 484 (490 on ondansetron in 07/2026); Mg 1.5, patient stopped Mg oxide; also on prochlorperazine and sertraline.
redFlags.implication: Torsades risk with QT prolonging drugs.
redFlags.action: Replete magnesium, avoid ondansetron, droperidol, and other QT prolonging antiemetics.

redFlags.finding: Very high PONV risk with limited antiemetic options
redFlags.evidence: Female, nonsmoker, prior severe PONV requiring admission, postop opioids; 5HT3 antagonists problematic.
redFlags.action: TIVA, dexamethasone, NK1 antagonist (aprepitant), scopolamine, opioid sparing regional (PECS).

redFlags.finding: Neutropenia and thrombocytopenia without a current count
redFlags.evidence: ANC 900 and Plt 112 on 10/24; oncology CBC for 10/26 not collected.
redFlags.implication: Infection and bleeding risk; regional block decisions.
redFlags.action: CBC with differential this morning; strict asepsis.

redFlags.finding: No IV access; left arm restricted, right arm is the surgical side
redFlags.evidence: Two failed attempts right arm; lymphedema left arm restriction; left IJ port present; port access not ordered.
redFlags.action: Access the port with sterile technique (order it), or lower extremity IV; avoid the left arm.

redFlags.implication: Anaphylaxis (about 1%) and falsely low pulse oximetry readings.
redFlags.action: Expect SpO2 artifact; be ready to treat anaphylaxis.

redFlags.implication: Avoid long acting relaxant or ensure reversal.
redFlags.action: LMA or short acting relaxant with full reversal before dissection.

planItems.item: Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
BP cuff on a leg or right arm before incision only per team; no left arm
Overnight observation with telemetry given QTc and EF
